subject.title: Node host: no SSH transport support + challenge auth fails behind reverse proxy

question: Should `openclaw node run` gain first-class managed SSH transport and remote-token pairing behavior, or should OpenClaw keep manual SSH tunnels as the supported node-host path while improving diagnostics/docs?
rationale: The choice changes how remote node hosts authenticate, how SSH tunnels are supervised, and whether a tunneled remote node is treated as local or remote for device/node pairing policy.

options.title: Define and implement remote node-host contract
options.body: Keep this issue open, coordinate the overlapping auth work with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91126, and require live reverse-proxy or tunnel proof before closing.

options.title: Split transport from auth policy
options.body: Track managed SSH for node-host separately and leave this issue focused on reverse-proxy pairing/auth once current-main live repro is available.

options.title: Keep manual SSH as supported path
options.body: Close only after maintainers explicitly decide not to manage node-host SSH transport in core and update docs/diagnostics to steer users to manual tunnels.

recommendation.title: Define and implement remote node-host contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, coordinate the overlapping auth work with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91126, and require live reverse-proxy or tunnel proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant node-host, gateway-client, SSH helper, and product-boundary history routes most strongly through this account.
